# PoseLoop v1.0.0 result summary

This report is rendered from
[`precomputed/v1.0.0/results.json`](../precomputed/v1.0.0/results.json).
It contains aggregate results only and requires no dataset, weights, GPU, or
third-party runtime.

## Results at a glance

| Phase | Scope | Result | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | 1 smoke sample | Runtime/checkpoint/evaluator evidence | No accuracy claim |
| M1 | 300 fixed targets | Combined `66.87%` | Single-view diagnostic baseline |
| **M2** | Same 300 targets, `k=5` | **`max_mask_area` `75.27%`, +8.40 pp** | **Main positive diagnostic** |
| M3 | 230-instance M2-disjoint holdout | Fast `83.69%` at 2.02 views, but -0.55 pp vs matched random | Budget saving; allocation hypothesis not supported |
| M4 | Same 230-instance holdout, one extra view | Learned `82.54%`: -0.63 pp vs target-only | No end-to-end gain; ranking advantage unresolved |

## M2: main positive diagnostic

On the same fixed 300-target oracle-mask subset as M1,
`max_mask_area` at `k=5` changes:

| Metric | Target-only | M2 selected | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| AR_MSSD | 63.30% | 72.53% | +9.23 pp |
| AR_MSPD | 70.43% | 78.00% | +7.57 pp |
| **Combined** | **66.87%** | **75.27%** | **+8.40 pp** |

The selector uses ground-truth visible-mask pixel count among already acquired views. The acquisition order is
target first, then fixed camera-centre greedy farthest-point order. This is a positive multi-view diagnostic, not an
independent holdout result or deployable selection policy. See the
[full M2 report](m2_multiview.md).

## M3: budget hypothesis not supported

The fast policy reaches 83.69% at
2.02 mean views and reduces recorded registration latency by
59.54% relative to fixed
`k=5`. It is nevertheless -0.55 pp below its
matched-random control; the paired 95% interval is
`[-3.18, +2.24 pp]`.

The conservative policy is -0.62 pp
below matched random, with paired 95% interval
`[-1.34, -0.07 pp]`. Thus M3
supports a budget/latency trade-off, but not a learned allocation advantage.
See the [full M3 report](m3_active_budget.md).

## M4: ranking hypothesis unresolved and no end-to-end gain

Learned VOI scores 82.54% macro combined:

| Comparison | Point estimate | Paired 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| vs target-only | -0.63 pp | `[-3.76, +2.50 pp]` |
| vs fixed-first | +0.44 pp | `[-1.45, +2.74 pp]` |
| vs random candidate | +1.45 pp | `[-0.31, +3.28 pp]` |

Every interval includes zero, and learned VOI remains below target-only. The
holdout contains 0 low-visibility
targets, so no low-visibility claim can be tested. See the
[full M4 report](m4_view_ranking.md).

## Scope and provenance

The reported combined metric is `oracle_mask_subset_ar_mssd_mspd`:
Mean of symmetry-aware AR_MSSD and AR_MSPD on the evaluated oracle visible-mask subset.

- Known object IDs and ground-truth visible masks are used.
- These are diagnostic subset results, not official BOP AP or full-dataset
  performance.
- M1/M2 share the same targets. M3/M4 share a
  physical-instance-disjoint-but-not-scene-disjoint holdout.
- M3/M4 use macro-object aggregation because holdout object counts are unequal.

Data attribution and third-party terms are documented in
[`LICENSES.md`](../LICENSES.md).
